notes: Upstream calls it their most powerful surface-recovery method and now recommends it; the tutorial's own fallback when it fails in a difficult region is GrowPatch, which is what seed-grow already does.

At the pinned commit fit_spiral.py is a research script, not a tool: no argparse, nine FIT_SPIRAL_* environment variables, and settings only through FIT_SPIRAL_CONFIG_OVERRIDES, whose 105 accepted keys upstream validates against its own default_config.

The scroll is not among those keys: dataset_path, scroll_name, z_begin/z_end, voxel_size_um and spiral_outward_sense are module-level constants assigned at import. It is selected here by rewriting those six assignments into a private copy of the script, located in the parse tree rather than by text, and read back before the run. The image keeps the bytes its source lock verified; the receipt carries the digest of the script before and after, and refuses the run if a constant is absent, shadowed or computed.

The adapter parses upstream's accepted keys out of the script with ast rather than importing it -- import executes module-level code that resolves dataset paths and opens Zarr groups -- and rejects an unknown override before a GPU is claimed instead of after.

Runs from the P1 queue on the spiral-fit lane, through framework/stages/01-segmentation/scripts/run_spiral_fit.py, in helena-villa-python -- the image that carries scripts/spiral and its Python dependencies. helena-villa is compiled binaries and cannot run it; a worker in the wrong runtime refuses by name before the lease.

Each fitted winding is published to the fleet's artifact store and registered with import_surface, the same route a grown surface takes, so P2's geometry certification and the lamina gate apply unchanged.
